title: Domain knowledge, explicit blind spots, and semantic school/life knowledge integration

sections.what: Add structured domain competence and explicit blind-spot modeling ({domain, level: ignorant|novice|familiar|expert, notes, jargon_terms}) unified with AgentMind semantic/procedural school, hobby, and parent-taught knowledge, and wire it into PromptBuilder, domain-gated item examination, jargon opacity, memory lifecycle dynamics, and the Persona editor.
sections.why: Right now PromptBuilder has 0 reads of player.skills, crafting_known, or player.get_knowledge_records(), causing agents to act uniformly omniscient (e.g. a legal specialist unpacking silicone curing physics or a skater casually discussing computer science). Representing whole English domain vocabularies per word would rot quickly, so domain proficiency plus explicit ignorance flags paired with optional specialist jargon terms, domain-gated examine layers, and semantic memory seeds makes asymmetrical knowledge real in simulation without unmaintainable word lists.
sections.how:
1. Add structured domains schema ({domain, level: ignorant|novice|familiar|expert, notes, jargon_terms}) under character capabilities/knowledge in engine/character_appearance.py, engine/character_store.py, player.py, and engine/serialization.py, alongside tagged semantic backstory seeds (school, family, hobby, trade) in player.memories (extending AgentMind / task-734 instead of creating a parallel database).
2. Wire PromptBuilder (CONTEXT_SECTIONS in static/js/agent/prompt-builder/context-sections.ts and character-state.ts) to render a concise knowledge & blind-spots section from player.domains, player.get_knowledge_records() (recipes/facts), and active skills so LLM agents stop operating at 0 knowledge visibility.
3. Extend engine/items/examine_actions.py (next to skill_check) with optional domain_notes / domain_min_level inspection layers so experts perceive technical diagnostics while ignorant observers receive layperson sensory descriptions, plus optional jargon-term opacity in listener comprehension for ignorant listeners.
4. Wire procedural disuse-decay tracking alongside non-decaying semantic school/life knowledge in engine/memory_dynamics.py and domain-tag boost in engine/memory_retrieval.py, plus Persona UI domain authoring controls in static/js/inspector/persona-view.ts.
sections.verify:
1. Run pytest covering domain competence/ignorance serialization, memory_dynamics semantic vs procedural decay curves, memory_retrieval domain boosts, and domain-gated examine_actions output.
2. Run npm run build:ts and JS unit tests verifying PromptBuilder CONTEXT_SECTIONS renders domains, explicit blind spots, and get_knowledge_records() without bloating prompts or breaking prose-only characters.

acceptance.text: Characters author and round-trip structured domain knowledge records ({domain, level, notes, jargon_terms}) including explicit ignorant blind spots across character_appearance.py, character_store.py, serialization.py, and Persona UI.

PromptBuilder CONTEXT_SECTIONS surfaces a compact knowledge & blind-spots fragment reading domain competence, active skills/recipes (player.get_knowledge_records()), and recalled semantic school/life/parent facts instead of leaving PromptBuilder at 0 readers.

Items support domain-gated examine layers in engine/items/examine_actions.py (experts see technical detail; ignorant observers see surface sensory fallback), and optional jargon_terms mask specialist terms for ignorant listeners.
engine/memory_dynamics.py completes task-734's semantic stability + procedural disuse-decay lifecycle for learned skills/recipes and school/parent knowledge.

custom.browser_ui:
Intended UI home: Character Inspector -> Mind -> Persona tab (Domains & Knowledge), Prompt Lens (CONTEXT_SECTIONS knowledge block), and examine action output.

Current availability: PromptBuilder has 0 references to player.skills, crafting_known, or get_knowledge_records(); Persona has no domain competence/ignorance editor; examine_actions.py only gates on dice skill_check without domain blind-spot layers.

Manual verification steps:
1. Open Zoe (diy_craft/silicone_molding=expert, sports=ignorant) and Kayla (law=expert, diy_craft=ignorant) in Mind -> Persona -> Capabilities/Knowledge and confirm domain rows round-trip across Save, Compile, and reload.
2. Inspect Zoe's and Kayla's Prompt Lens context.
   - expected: Each character's prompt includes their active domains, skills/recipes, school/parent semantic seeds, and explicit ignorant blind spots.
3. Have both characters examine a two-part platinum silicone mold kit authored with domain_notes.
   - expected: Zoe reads curing/sulfur-inhibition detail while Kayla sees a layperson surface description.
